rules: Each entry is a dated operational source claim, not proof that an area has been exhaustively searched or cleared.
Search, rescue, recovery, road clearance, relief, family tracing, infrastructure assessment, sanitation and risk monitoring are distinct categories.
A location may have multiple simultaneous activities and multiple source claims.
Completed activity at one named site must not be generalized to the surrounding district.
Person-status conclusions must come from person-level evidence, not from operational activity alone.

activities.activity: National search and rescue operations continued with Nepal Army, Nepal Police, Armed Police Force and other responders; operations had resumed after weather and secondary-flood concerns.
Search efforts were focused on the hydropower project, including a mud-filled tunnel where more than 100 people were feared trapped; tunnel rescues were reported as part of the wider operation.
Sixteen Nepal Army and private-sector helicopters were operating shuttle flights through these locations for evacuation, rescue and supply movement.
Road connectivity to Rasuwa was restored through the Bogatitar–Kalikasthan–Dhunche route, reconnecting the district to the national road network for small four-wheeled vehicles.
Authorities were clearing mud and flood debris from a remaining constrained section of the Prithvi Highway near Baireni Bazaar; excavators were deployed and traffic was progressively restored.
Road clearance at Devighat was reported completed.
Heavy equipment was mobilized to remove flood debris and restore transport services along the corridor.
A hill excavator, loader and tipper were deployed for road clearance.
Three heavy-equipment units were deployed for obstruction removal and road restoration.
A backhoe was deployed and an additional wheel loader was being arranged from the Nuwakot Road Division.
Nepal Red Cross established a Restoring Family Links help desk to help affected people contact relatives by phone.
activities.source_name: Nepal Red Cross Society Situation Report #2

activities.activity: Fifteen Nepal Red Cross volunteers were oriented on Initial Rapid Assessment and mobilized for affected-area data collection.
activities.source_name: Nepal Red Cross Society Situation Report #2

activities.activity: Nepal Red Cross distributed ready-to-eat food to 750 people across Kriyaputri Bhawan, Yoga Kendra, Ayurvedic Hospital, Chandra Jyoti school and Trisuli Bazar, with blankets and mattresses also distributed at selected sites.
Nepal Red Cross volunteers were supporting meal management and shelter populations at Ayurvedic Hospital, Archale, Chaapdanda, Bidur Kriyaputri shelter and Yogbhawan shelter.

activities.location: Roads · bridges · electricity · drinking water · telecommunications · hydropower
activities.activity: Fifteen technical teams and sectoral groups were deployed for a comprehensive damage assessment across critical infrastructure sectors.
Authorities reported arrangements for drinking water, fuel and sanitation as part of the post-disaster response.
Authorities continued monitoring for a possible fresh flood and urged people in risk locations to move to safe areas.

activities.location: Nepal disaster response and consular network
activities.activity: Special coordination continued for search, rescue and identification of foreign nationals through Nepal's Ministry of Foreign Affairs Emergency Control Room, embassies and families.
Chitwan had the largest reported downstream body-recovery count in the 29 August NDRRMA update, indicating a major recovery and identification workload downstream from the source area.
Large downstream body-recovery numbers were reported, making this a major recovery and identification location rather than only a distant impact district.
Downstream body recovery continued in Dhading while road clearance and access restoration were also underway on major transport corridors.
